items.title: 67426_Hayes Pillars oral history interview
items.q: She came to St. Louis and we rehearsed

ctx.x: That was the Gingham Inn, wasn't it?

Gingham Inn, yes. We played about three and a half -- about three weeks. And they closed -- and the place closed down. So the owners decided to keep our band do -- together, they secured the services of a young lady named Jean Calloway. Jean Calloway had a nice voice and she could front a band. And back in those days the word Calloway was pretty hot. So, they sent for Jean Calloway to come to St. Louis. She came to St. Louis and we rehearsed and, in the meantime, we augmented the band by sending to Kansas City…

George came and joined the band. Mr. Pitts left the band, we sent and got Walter Page on bass. To join the band. Our piano player left the band, Mr. Goodman, -- Goodson, so we hired a piano player in St. Louis, by the name of --
